brief.scope: Code audit PR #57 lane/skeptic-write 75c4428 vs origin/dev. Codex check-tests gets out/ writable_roots and TMPDIR under out/ while the snapshot stays read-only; wait classifies closed envelope=invalid as envelope not wall. Review only.

findings.claim: The out/ write grant is hardcoded to job == 'check-tests', but plan (deliverable out/PLAN.md) and adjudicate (out/RULING.md) are also read-role Codex jobs whose deliverables live under out/ and hit the identical read-only wall. The plan slice's own Contract item 1 states the rule generally ('A Codex job whose deliverable is a file under the job out/ directory must pass out/ in writable_roots'), yet the implementation fixes exactly one of N identical cases, and the pre-existing test_launch_isolation.py:88-94 positively asserts that plan+codex must NOT carry writable_roots. So the codebase now holds two opposite answers for the same situation: either plan/adjudicate on Codex remain unable to write their deliverables (unfixed, and a test locks the breakage in), or read-only Codex could already write out/ and the new grant is a no-op. The change resolves neither. This is a declared-vs-practiced gap (general contract, check-tests-only practice).
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'writable_out=rec\["job"\] == "check-tests"' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py; sed -n '84,95p' ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/test_launch_isolation.py; sed -n '55,95p' ops/devlane/task/jobs.json  # plan/adjudicate deliverables under out/, granted no writable_roots

findings.where: ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py:424 (if sandbox == "workspace-write" or writable_out) and :782-785 (TMPDIR under out/); ops/devlane/dispatch/tests/test_launch_skeptic_write.py (whole)
findings.claim: The fix's whole mechanism — pass sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots while keeping --sandbox read-only — is a load-bearing vendor coupling with no probe verifying the live surface, contrary to docs/verified-couplings.md and AGENTS.md ('no vendor becomes load-bearing'). Codex consults sandbox_workspace_write.* only when the effective policy is workspace-write; under --sandbox read-only the writable_roots list is not part of the policy, so out/SKEPTIC.md and the TMPDIR under out/tmp would still be denied — exactly the failure records bb30da/bb8ddb described. The two new tests (test_launch_skeptic_write.py) assert only argv tokens and env presence; neither proves Codex can actually write under this argv. Nothing in the slice looked at real Codex write behavior — this is 'could not look' presented as a confident answer (docs/wire.md absence discipline, docs/probes.md). Impact if the assumption is wrong: the slice does not unblock check-tests at all.
findings.reproduce: python3 -m unittest discover -s ops/devlane/dispatch/tests -p test_launch_skeptic_write.py  # passes on argv shape only. Live check (cannot run here): codex exec --sandbox read-only -c 'sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots=["/tmp/outdir"]' with a prompt to write /tmp/outdir/x — observe whether the write is permitted or refused; no such probe or verified mock exists in the tree (rg -n 'writable_roots' ops --glob '!*.py' returns nothing).

findings.claim: The new wall classification keys solely on returncode == 2, but `launch.py` returns exit 2 for two unrelated conditions: `_wait` timeout (launch.py:1623, the genuine wall) AND the generic exception handler in main() (launch.py:1760-1762, RuntimeError/OSError/ValueError/JSONDecodeError). An internal error raised during wait therefore reaches the operator labelled 'wall' — a timeout that never happened — hiding the real fault. The plan's Contract item 2 defines wall narrowly as 'wait exits because elapsed >= timeout while the record is still not closed'; keying on an overloaded exit code widens it. (Note: launch.py refusals exit REFUSAL=3, so those land in the 'died' branch instead — also imprecise, but less misleading than reporting a wall.)
findings.reproduce: sed -n '1620,1624p' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py  # timeout: return 2; sed -n '1760,1762p' ops/devlane/dispatch/launch.py  # generic error: return 2; sed -n '820,821p' ops/conductor/tools/ladder.py  # both map to reason=wall

envelope.note: Adversarial code audit of PR #57 lane/skeptic-write, commit 75c4428 vs c715b24 (aimed at origin/dev). Method: read the whole diff (context/diff.patch) and the input slice (in/slice-skeptic-write.md), then the reviewed sources in the snapshot — launch.py _argv/_run_attempt/_wait/main, ladder.py await_result, jobs.json, test_launch_isolation.py, and the two new test files. The wait-reason change (ladder.py) is correct for the three real close/died/timeout cases and the fix genuinely stops stderr 'running' poll lines from forcing 'wall'; my only wait finding is the residual returncode==2 overload (Finding 3, confirmed against launch.py exit paths). The writable-out change verifies clean at the argv level and the tests pass, but the two strongest findings are about what the tests cannot see: an in-repo contradiction (Finding 1, confirmed — plan/adjudicate treated opposite to check-tests) and an unverified read-only+writable_roots vendor coupling (Finding 2, plausible — I could not execute Codex here, so this is declared as could-not-look, not proven-broken; if the Codex assumption is wrong the slice fails its purpose, a p1 impact held at p2 pending a probe). Verdict changes: at minimum the change needs a probe proving Codex honors writable_roots under --sandbox read-only, and a stated reason why plan/adjudicate are left unfixed. Spend left as the launcher sentinel per brief.
